senses.gloss: स्कन्ध- + चाप स्कन्ध- + चाप, m. a sort of yoke for carrying burthens.
स्कन्ध- + वाह स्कन्ध- + वाह, m. an ox of burthen.
स्कन्ध- + वाहक स्कन्ध- + वाहक, m. an ox of burthen.
स्कन्ध- + शाखा स्कन्ध- + शाखा, f. the principal branch of a tree.

1. स्कन्द् स्कन्द्, i. 1, Par.
 1. To jump.
 2. To jump upwards, to ascend.
 3. To burst out, MBh. 1, 5105.
 4. To jump downward, to drop, to fall, Bhaṭṭ. 22, 11.
 5. To perish, Man. 7, 84.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. स्कन्न.
 1. Trickled down, Rām. 1, 38, 27.
 2. Sprinkled, MBh. 1, 2434.
 3. Fallen.
 --Caus.
 1. To emit (the seminal fluid), Man. 2, 180; 9, 150.
 2. To neglect. Man. 6, 9.
 --With the prep. अव अव, To assail, to besiege, Śiś. 1, 51.
 --With अभ्यव अभि-अव, To jump out, MBh. 4, 810.
 --With समव सम्-अव, Caus. To assail, Man. 7, 196.
 --With आ आ, To assail, Mālat. 151, 9; Bhaṭṭ. 17, 11.
 --With समा सम्-आ, To assail, Bhaṭṭ. 16, 10. []
 --With परि परि, स्कन्द् and ष्कन्द्, To spring about, Bhaṭṭ. 9, 75.
 --With प्र प्र,
 1. To spring forward, MBh. 1, 134; to spring down, 3, 15587.
 2. To burst forth, MBh. 1, 2380. प्रस्कन्न, Fallen. m. A sinner, one who has violated the usages of his caste.
 --Caus. To cross (a river), MBh. 4, 1971.
 --Cf. Lat. scandere; σκάνδαλον, σχαστήο (χ for κ by the influence of σ), probably σκάζω.
† 2. स्कन्द् स्कन्द्, स्कन्ध् स्कन्ध्, i. 10, Par. To collect.

स्कन्द 1. स्कन्द् + अ, m.
 1. Skanda or Kārttikeya, the god of war, Megh. 44.
 2. A king.
 3. The body.
 4. The bank of a river.
 5. A clever man (cf. स्कन्ध).
 6. A proper name, Rājat. 5, 417 (or घ्राणस्कन्द).
स्कन्दक स्कन्द + क, m. A soldier, Rājat. 5, 174.

स्कन्दन स्कन्द् + अन, n.
 1. Effusion.
 2. Purging.
 3. Going.

स्कन्ध स्कन्ध,
 I. m.
 1. The shoulder, Pañc. 144, 23.
 2. The body, Mālat. 84, 17.
 3. The trunk of a tree, Pañc. iii. d. 149.
 4. A branch, Pañc. 134, 5.
 5. A branch of human knowledge.
 6. A book, Bhāg. P. i. ii., etc.
 7. The five objects of sense.
 8. The five forms of mundane consciousness, in the Bauddha philosophy, Śiś. 2, 26; cf. Burnouf, Introd. à l'Hist. du Buddh. 475.
 9. A road.
 10. Part of an army.
 11. War.
 12. A multitude.
 13. An agreement.
 14. A king.
 15. A wise or learned man.
 16. A heron.
 II. f. धा.
 1. A branch.
 2. A creeper.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. A.S. sculdor, sculder; O.H.G. scultarra; probably σπάθη; Lat. scapula (for old scaphula, cf. rufus, s. v. रुधिर, and rutilus, ib. for old ruthilus).
स्कन्ध- + स्कन्ध स्कन्ध- + स्कन्ध (repeated), m. every shoulder, Kām. Nītis. 9, 19 (where the visarga must be erased), Hit. iv. d. 122, v. r.

स्कन्धस् स्कन्धस्, n.
 1. The shoulder.
 2. The trunk of a tree (cf. the last).

स्कन्धावार स्कन्धावार, i. e. स्कन्ध-आ-वृ + अ, m.
 1. An army, or division of it attached to the king.
 2. A royal residence.
 3. A camp, Hit. 107, 21; MBh. 1, 6950.
स्कन्धिक स्कन्धिक, i. e. स्कन्ध + इक, m. An ox of burthen.
स्कन्धिन् स्कन्धिन्, i. e. स्कन्ध + इन्, m. A tree.
स्कन्धोपनेय स्कन्धोपनेय, i. e. स्कन्ध-उप-नेय (vb. नी), adj. m. (viz. संधि), A form of peace-offering in which fruit or grain is presented as token of submission, Hit. iv. d. 122.

स्कम्भ् स्कम्भ्, i. 1, Ātm., ii. 5, स्कभ्नु and 9, स्कभ्ना, नी, Par.
 1. To make firm (to create), Bhāg. P. 2, 7, 40.
 2. To support (ved.).
 3. To stop, to obstruct, to impede.
 --With the prep. वि वि, Caus. विष्कम्भित,
 1. Impeded, shown away, Pañc. 29, 6.
 2. Obstructed, [] precluded, Pañc. 56, 10.
 --Cf. स्तम्भ् and स्तम्ब; Lat. scabellum, scamnum; Goth. ga-skapjan, ga-skafts; A.S. scapen, sceápan, sceaft; O.H.G. scafan, scafôn, scoppôn, to stop; probably σκῆπτρον, σκήπτω, σκίμπτω.
